title: SSO/SAML: IdP interoperability checks, fixes, and admin playbook
creator: Alexandra Kim
description: Scope: Validate and harden SSO/SAML flows across major IdPs (Okta, Azure AD, Google Workspace, Ping Identity) for RBAC v2 and admin controls; implement fixes for interoperability gaps; produce an operator-facing admin playbook and end-to-end configuration docs. Deliverables: 1) IdP compatibility matrix with reproducible test cases and known workarounds; 2) Code fixes and configuration changes for SAML assertions/attribute mappings and ACS/RelayState behaviors; 3) Admin onboarding playbook (step-by-step Okta/Azure/Google/Ping templates, common troubleshooting); 4) QA test harness and automated integration tests for CI; 5) Release notes and runbook for customer success/solutions engineers. Motivation: Several enterprise customers reported login failures and incorrect role mapping after RBAC v2 rollout. Root causes include attribute name normalization differences, unexpected encrypted assertions, and RelayState handling in some IdP integrations. This ticket coordinates engineering fixes, compatibility docs, and release gating for the security-2026.03 milestone.
acceptance_criteria: Matrix created: for each IdP list supported SAML features, required attribute names, supported signing/encryption profiles, RelayState behavior, and known caveats
Automated integration tests added to CI that run SAML flow simulations for Okta/Azure/Google/Ping (pass rate >= 95%)
All critical interoperability bugs fixed or documented with supported workarounds
Admin playbook published in Confluence and linked from Console onboarding; includes screenshots and templated metadata XML for each IdP
Security review completed and approvals recorded; no regressions to RBAC enforcement in staging
tests: Run SAML assertions through local SAML test harness (samltest.org style) for each IdP profile
Simulate signed-only, signed+encrypted, and unsigned assertions and verify role mapping behavior
Validate RelayState round-trip with and without HTTP-POST bindings
End-to-end smoke test: create user in IdP, assert role attribute, login via SAML to staging, verify RBAC v2 scoped permissions
CI job: nightly SSO compatibility run against stage environment with recorded results uploaded to security dashboard
implementation_notes: Normalize incoming SAML attribute keys: map common variants (e.g., 'groups', 'group', 'memberOf', 'roles') into canonical 'redwood_roles' attribute before RBAC evaluation
Add optional lenient parsing mode behind a feature flag to prevent breakage for customers with nonstandard attribute formats
Ensure ACS endpoint accepts both HTTP-POST and HTTP-Redirect bindings and correctly processes RelayState per IdP behavior
Support XML encrypted assertion decryption in runtime path; fall back with clear logging and guidance if KMS keys are not configured
Update metadata validator to detect common Okta/Azure misconfigurations (certificate chain format, AssertionConsumerService index mismatch)
Create example IdP JSON and raw XML samples to include in Confluence templates
risks: Encrypted assertions require KMS/HSM access; customers without KMS may not be able to use that mode
Lenient parsing increases risk of accidentally accepting malformed attributes; will gate via feature flag and audit logs
Edge-case RelayState implementations can break SSO flows for older IdP installations; may require per-customer fixes
Automated tests may not fully capture network-level SAML oddities seen in customer-managed IdPs
